newsitem.title: HONG KONG: UK's Rifkind to press China on world court - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK's Rifkind to press China on world court - paper.

text.p: British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind said London would ask China to agree to allow the world court to rule on the legality of Hong Kong's controversial provisional legislature later this month.

In an interview with a Hong Kong Chinese-language newspaper published on Wednesday, Rifkind said he would raise the issue with Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen during a meeting in Singapore next week.
Rifkind told the Sing Tao newspaper in London that Britain made the offer last October, but China had refused. He hoped China would reconsider the proposal.
The minister said Britain needed Beijing's approval for the request, otherwise the International Court of Justice at The Hague would not accept the request.

China, angered by Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten's democratic reforms in the dying days of British rule, formed an interim assembly to replace Hong Kong's current elected legislature after the colony returns to Beijing's control on July 1.
Britain and Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp condemn the move, saying Beijing's plan breaches the 1984 Sino-British agreement which sets the framework for the return of the territory to China.
The provisional legislature held its first meeting last month in Shenzhen, across the border from Hong Kong, to avoid legal challenges to its legitimacy in the territory.
Rifkind also said he would discuss China's recent plan to roll back civil liberties in Hong Kong after the handover.
He said China had no understanding of the concept of a free society and therefore could not understand the damage that would be inflicted by the proposed changes.

A Beijing-appointed Preparatory Committee, overseeing the transfer of sovereignty, recently voted to scrap a number of Hong Kong laws including legislation that protects human rights and basic political freedoms in the territory of 6.3 million people.
